hypotheses.root_cause: A dependency cycle on NoC ring R1 (around the PCIE<->DDR routes) deadlocked the fabric, so the DMA->PCIE transaction 0xE470 timed out and the interconnect failed.
hypotheses.rationale: The first warning in the run is 'NOC: WARN: Dependency cycle suspected | ring=R1 members=2' at 3921 ms. This is the catalogue's tell-tale for RC_NOC_DEADLOCK. It is followed by repeated congestion warnings (txn_q=high, stall_pct 26-33%) on PCIE<->DDR and CPU<->DDR up to 4388 ms. The DMA->PCIE timeout comes at 4738 ms and the fatal error at 4799 ms. Nothing in the logs points to QoS starvation (no credits=0 or credit-starvation lines) or DMA burst overflow (no burst_len lines), even though the two most similar past incidents had those causes. Points against: fabric stall had dropped to 1-13% in the last 250 ms before the timeout, which doesn't fit a fabric-wide deadlock unless the stuck flows stayed confined to ring R1. PCIe retrain count also climbed steadily (41->44 in about 150 ms) on the destination link. A flaky PCIe link could be causing or adding to the timeout, so confidence is moderate. The register dump is raw hex and I couldn't decode it.
recommended_actions: Decode the NOC0 register snapshot and check the R1 ring route table for a cyclic channel dependency between the 2 members (PCIE<->DDR paths)
Enable deadlock-recovery / escape-VC timeouts on ring R1 and rerun the same traffic to see if the timeout goes away
Rule out the PCIe link: pin the link at a lower gen or turn off ASPM, track LTSSM retrain events, and check whether the retrain count rising lines up with the DMA->PCIE stalls
Rerun with DMA->PCIE traffic isolated from CPU/DDR traffic to confirm the failure needs the cross-route dependency
